records.question: Approximately what percentage of Tutuila's coast is bordered by a fringing reef?
ground_truth_chunks: Of the 125 km of coast (78 mi.) approximately 60% is bordered by a fringing reef and about 20% of the natural coast was fronted by beach (much of this coast is now fronted by engineering structures).

records.section_heading: CHARACTERISTICS OF THE NATURAL COASTAL SYSTEM
records.question: What are the two primary types of coastline on Tutuila?
records.ground_truth_answer: The two primary types of coastline on Tutuila are: (a) depositional coasts consisting of coastal plains, beaches, wetlands and mangrove forests, and (b) erosional coasts characterized by seacliffs.
ground_truth_chunks: There are two primary types of coastline on Tutuila: a) depositional coasts consisting of coastal plains, beaches, wetlands and mangrove forests, and b) erosional coasts characterized by seacliffs.

Although there is overlap between the two, such as a cliffed coast fronted by a narrow cobble or sand beach, in general they are distinguishable. Moreover, a beach undergoing erosion is still primarily a depositional feature.

records.question: Which coast of Tutuila is described as being mostly cliffed with little or no fringing reef development?
records.ground_truth_answer: Most of the north coast of Tutuila is cliffed with little or no fringing reef development.
ground_truth_chunks: Most of the north coast of Tutuila is cliffed with little or no fringing reef development with the exception of the deep embayments at Aoa, Masefau, Afono, Vatia, Fagasa, Fagafue, Aasu, Aoloau, and Maloata.
The south coast is also cliffed however, in general, the cliffs are lower, less rugged, and interrupted by more prominent valley development than along the north coast.

records.section_heading: Area 2: Breakers point to Cape Matatula
records.question: Which segment of Area 2 represents the longest, relatively undisturbed, open-coast sandy shoreline on Tutuila?
ground_truth_chunks: 2) Matuli Point to Cape Matatula. This area does not contain any of the offshore inventory sites but it is extremely important as a coastal site because it represents the longest, relatively undisturbed, opencoast sandy shoreline on Tutuila.
A gently-curved carbonate sand beach extends about 2 km from Lealaeli Hill to Fagasa Point (Plate 4).

records.question: What is the dominant beach sediment within Leone Bay and how does it differ from other beaches in Area 5?
records.ground_truth_answer: Terrigenous sand is the dominant beach sediment within Leone Bay, whereas carbonate sand predominates along the other beaches.

records.section_heading: Area 7: Fogagogo to Breakers Pt. (excluding Pago Pago Harbor).
records.question: What is the net longshore drift direction of the Coconut Pt. barrier spit in Area 7?
ground_truth_chunks: The Coconut Pt. barrier spit is composed mostly of carbonate sand and the morphology indicates a growth direction (net longshore drift direction) from northeast to southwest.
Most of the seaward edge of the spit shoreline is undergoing erosion with rates of 1 to 1.5 m/yr in the south and about 0.5 m/yr in the north (U.S. Army Corps of Engineers, 1980, 1989).

records.question: What is the width of the fringing reef adjacent to Site 3 (Aua)?
ground_truth_chunks: Adjacent Reef Characteristics: The fringing reef is up to 300 m wide and a small patch reef, Amu'ula Rock, occurs offshore. The inner reef flat is covered by sediment. The seaward edge of the reef flat is highly irregular, probably due to freshwater outflow of the streams.
